title: Adaptive Slowpath Queue with Per-Tenant Throughput Guardrails and Opportunistic Demotion
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Background: Customers on Redwood Dedicated request predictable throughput for committed tenants while workloads have bursty tail patterns. Existing admission shapers provide hard caps and broad shedding policies, but we've observed QoS cliffs for long-running tokens and unfairness when a few tenants spike. This ticket designs and implements an adaptive slowpath queue that provides soft per-tenant throughput guardrails, opportunistic demotion (best-effort degradation to lower-cost execution lanes), and autoscaler hooks so fleet scaling respects committed minima and burst escrow. The aim is to avoid wholesale rejections while preserving headroom for high-priority traffic and predictable unit economics.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant committed throughput (RPS or token/s) can be configured and enforced as a soft guarantee with measurable reservation usage exposed in Console
Under 95th percentile load spikes, high-priority tenants maintain at least 75% of their committed throughput and see no >10x increase in p99 latency compared to baseline
Opportunistic demotion moves degraded requests to lower-cost execution lanes without altering user-facing semantics (no silent truncation) and can be toggled via feature flag
Autoscaler exposes a signal (slowpath backlog size and committed-reservation deficit) that increases desired capacity when sustained deficit > 30s
Observability: dashboards for per-tenant reservation usage, slowpath queue length, demotion rate, and reject/shed events are live; alerts fire when demotion > 10% of requests for >5min
Integration tests and load harness reproduce a tenant burst scenario and show graceful degradation with no outage-level errors
design_decisions: Soft guarantees implemented as token escrow: each tenant has a provisioned-min pool plus a burst escrow funded by recent idle capacity. Escrow decays over a configurable window
Slowpath queue is per-fleet but implements tenant-weighted fairness with a per-tenant windowed deficit counter to prefer tenants close to their committed levels
Opportunistic demotion routes requests to pre-configured lower-cost model variants or quantized shards; demotion respects compatibility matrix to avoid semantic regressions
Admission controls expose a backpressure header for SDKs (X-Redwood-Backpressure-Hint) so clients may adopt exponential retry/backoff patterns
Autoscaler hook: a new metric (committed_deficit_seconds) is emitted; cluster autoscaler will multiply deficit by a configurable headroom factor to drive scale-up decisions
We opt for conservative defaults: demotion disabled for P0 customers, escrow windows default to 60s, and slowpath max depth has a hard cap to prevent memory blowups
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype slowpath queue and per-tenant deficit counter in staging; implementation in admission-proxy with in-memory footprint and sharded maps
Phase 2: Add token escrow accounting and integration with per-tenant config service; surface reservation usage in Console API
Phase 3: Implement demotion routing rules and compatibility checks; add model-variant mapping in routing catalog
Phase 4: Emit autoscaler metrics and wire a simple rule in K8s autoscaler integration for Dedicated clusters
Phase 5: End-to-end testing, chaos tests (killing model workers), and load tests against production-like fleet sizes
Phase 6: Gradual rollout behind feature flag and monitor metrics; iterate on thresholds
rollout_plan: Gate behind feature flag in admission-proxy and routing; initially enable for internal tenants and a small set of opt-in customers (5%)
Day-0 Canary: route 1-2 Dedicated hosts through new slowpath in a single region, monitor latency, queue depth, and rejections
Week-1: Increase to 20% of Dedicated fleet for non-P0 tenants; gather feedback and adjust escrow decay and demotion thresholds
Week-2: Open to larger cohorts and enable autoscaler hook in read-only mode (emit metrics but do not scale) to observe signal quality
Full rollout only after 2 weeks of stable signals and sign-off from SRE and Product
